title: Webb: unfold, cool, focus
subtitle: The engineering behind a cold infrared observatory: a deployable mirror, a thermal barrier and months of optical alignment.
description: The engineering behind a cold infrared observatory: a deployable mirror, a thermal barrier and months of optical alignment.

elements.text: A large mirror on the cold side
Unfolding creates an observatory that could never fit inside its rocket.

segments act as
one 6.5 m mirror

Support struts unfold
in front of the primary.
An infrared telescope must stay cold enough to detect faint signals.
Vacuum gaps limit conduction; separated membranes radiate heat outward.
Its mid-infrared detectors operate near 7 K, colder than passive cooling alone can provide.
Deploy first. Then turn eighteen images into one.
Physical deployment ends before optical commissioning is complete.

Fold the mirror and shield
inside the launch envelope.

Extend and tension the shield;
open the secondary and wings.

Align the segment images
and phase the primary mirror.

One aligned aperture
feeds the science instruments.
